Note::rstrip¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signatures¶

Note Note::rstrip() const
Note Note::rstrip(std::string_view chars) const

Trim Characters From The End Of Every Cell¶

rstrip() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with trailing whitespace removed from each cell; rstrip(chars) instead removes any character that appears in the chars set from the end. It is the right-only half of strip — use it to drop a trailing newline, a padding run, or a stray delimiter while leaving the start of the cell intact.

The no-argument form trims the ASCII whitespace bytes space, \t, \n, \r, \f, \v. rstrip(chars) treats chars as a set of bytes: positions at the end whose byte is in the set are removed until a byte that is not is reached. Pass only ASCII characters in chars. A cell made entirely of trimmable characters becomes "".

rstrip is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: Trim Trailing Whitespace¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"  hello  ", "\tworld\t", "clean"}).rstrip())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["  hello", "\tworld", "clean"]

The leading whitespace is kept; only the right side is trimmed.

See Also¶

  • Note::lstrip: the left-only counterpart.

  • Note::strip: both ends.

  • Note::remove_suffix: remove one occurrence of a fixed string, not a character set.
